handled_verified.description: Node types the analyzer reads and emits from, each pinned by a fixture in validation/m14/fixtures/nim/ (5 pass, every fixture source accepted by the Nim 2.2.12 compiler), by the 15-check index seam in script/m14/verify-nim-pipeline-e2e.ts, or by the NIM differential lane in script/m14/differential.ts (nim@60 941/941 covered, MISSING=0, unexplained=0%; pixie@60 3220/3220, MISSING=0, unexplained=0%). The declaration types are the whole surface: proc/func/method/iterator/template/macro/converter _declaration, type_declaration, variable_declaration with its const/let/var/using _section, object_declaration, enum_declaration, concept_declaration, and field_declaration / enum_field_declaration / variant_discriminator_declaration members; the call types are call and dot_generic_call; the rest are the name-, path- and argument-bearing payload nodes reached through grammar FIELDS (name, body, pragmas, module, operator, left, right, function, first_argument, type, items, source) or through node types. M14 NIM wave: no node type is matched by a source-text prefix (the analyzer contains no RegExp at all), and no field is read that the pinned grammar does not declare. Two families were found by the differential rather than by inspection and are the reason this list is evidence-backed rather than asserted: a destructuring binding (tuple_deconstruct_declaration wrapping symbol_declaration) never entered its scope frame, so a read was misattributed to a same-named struct property; and a path deeper than two segments was dropped whole because the grammar models the separator as a named `operator` node whose text is the entire token.

internal_silent.description: Container, literal, comment and payload nodes that correctly emit no symbol and no relationship: they are reached by the walk and carry nothing the taxonomy has a row for. Three of these deserve the reason spelled out, because "unreferenced" is not the same as "ignored": (1) field_declaration_list and variant_declaration — a `case` block's fields are field_declaration INSIDE the variant_declaration, and the field rule emits them, so the container itself is silent while its members are handled (verified: a variant object emits properties isCircle, radius, side, name, plainField); (2) pragma_expression — a pragma wrapped around an expression contributes only its arguments, and the declaration-level pragmas are read from the `pragmas` FIELD, so this node type is a second route to the same names rather than a missing one; (3) tuple_construction — an anonymous tuple value has no name to resolve, so there is nothing for `instantiates` to point at (a NAMED construction, `TypeName(field: v)`, is handled and is the shape the corpus exercises 93 times). The literal set (integer/float/char/nil/custom_numeric/generalized_string and their content and escape payloads) emits nothing by contract: a literal value is not a declaration and its text is not a name. The bare-statement set (assembly, bind, discard, mixin, raise, return, static, yield) declares nothing; `return`/`raise`/`yield` carry no reference the analyzer would invent a target for.

gap.description: No confirmed analyzer gap: every one of the 127 named types the pinned wasm declares is either handled or a silent container, and the differential reports MISSING=0 and unexplained=0 in both directions on both corpora. The OPEN work in this lane is a GRAMMAR gap, which is a different ledger: 11 named node types are never reached because the pinned grammar cannot parse the construct that would produce them (do-pragma is consumed as a block comment, so no pragma node appears; a multi-line leading-dot chain, nested bracket generics `f[A, seq[B]]`, a single-line `if cond: stmt`, a `$` inside a string literal, a command-style call with a multi-line argument, a qualified type in a declaration, a pragma on a generic parameter, `func(…)` as a type, an empty tuple `(;)` and a bare-identifier tuple construction). Those are recorded in docs/analyzers/real-nim-analyzer.md with their site counts and named classes, and a 56-line do-pragma patch is preserved unapplied at $HOME/fixtures/nim/out/0001-nim-dopragma.patch because a rebuilt wasm has not yet passed the 72-case conformance suite, the 17-file compiler matrix and the corpus regression.

design_decision.description: Owner rulings. Each is a deliberate refusal to publish, not a silence.

decisions.question: A file-scope pragma statement (`{.push checks: off.}`, `{.warning: nil.}`) names pragmas that the analyzer does not publish anywhere. Should it?
decisions.resolution: No, and the reason is that the taxonomy has no row for a file-scope decorator: the symbols row is per declaration, and a pragma statement is not a declaration. The pragma NAMES that matter are already published — as `decorators` on each declaration that carries its own `pragmas` field, which is where they have an effect. Publishing the file-scope statement as well would produce a row whose target is a name no symbol declares, i.e. a dangling edge on purpose. Left RULED rather than silent so that the absence is a decision on the record.

decisions.question: An `overrides` edge needs the project-wide type hierarchy. The analyzer is per-file. Resolve against a corpus-wide name set?
decisions.resolution: No. A same-named method on an unrelated type is a collision, and emitting the edge would assert an inheritance relation the source never states. `overrides` is emitted only when the base is declared in the same file, which is what the fixture, the seam and the targeted 71-file method-heavy draw exercise (40 overrides, matching on both sides). The cross-file case is a declared limit of a per-file analyzer, not a gap to be papered over with a wider name set.

decisions.question: Nim has `concept`, which looks like an interface, and the base ontology has an `implements` relationship. Does a concept satisfaction emit it?
decisions.resolution: No. A concept is satisfied by implicit structural dispatch, and Nim has no nominal subtype declaration to point at, so there is no name in the file that says "X implements Y" — the fact is computed by the compiler from the method set. A concept DECLARATION is emitted as a SymbolKind.Interface symbol (it is the structural contract), but no relationship is invented for satisfaction. The differential reports the label vacuous (0 truth, 0 analyzer) rather than pretending it is covered.

decisions.question: The grammar's own file-types declares `nimble`, and .nimble files are real NIM source. Route them to the nim analyzer?
decisions.resolution: Not yet, and not on the strength of the grammar's file-types list. A .nimble is a package manifest with `requires`/`task`/`bin` blocks whose surface is not the module surface this analyzer models, and the corpus scan already shows what routing on grammar metadata alone buys: 171 tracked .nimble files whose parse health has never been measured. So the decision waits for a measurement, and the corpus record notes the 171 files as excluded from the complexity artifact (5,056 .nim/.nims files measured, 5,227 total in the parse record) rather than quietly reporting one number as if it covered both.

decisions.question: `.nims` is a Nim configuration script, in the grammar's file-types and produced by 35 tracked files in the corpus. Route it?
decisions.resolution: Not in production yet, but it is measured: the differential lane's ext list carries `nim,nims` so the sweep does not silently skip it, and the corpus parse record counts its files. What is missing is a routing decision backed by a parse-health number for the extension alone, which is why it stays out of language-detection.ts rather than being guessed at. The measured `nim+nims` counts per repo are in the corpus artifact.
